task_instance: Using the vr-ar skill's principles, write a VR design spec for a small standalone-headset + browser-kiosk museum experience ('Tide Pools'), pinning down platform choice, comfort/locomotion, performance budget, interaction model, spatial scale, UI and an anti-pattern checklist from a one-paragraph project brief.
evidence: The skill is a pure principles/reference document (allowed-tools Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep; no bundled scripts, SDKs, models or external services to invoke). Its core deliverable is applying the stated VR/AR principles. Created a sample input brief at brief.md and produced the deliverable at tide-pools-vr-design-spec.md. Verified the spec against every section of SKILL.md: Platform Selection (chose Quest standalone + WebXR browser, dropped PCVR/PSVR), Comfort (teleport + snap turn for locomotion, vignette, seated/standing, height calibration, no camera shake, gradual acceleration), Performance (Quest 3 target 90 FPS and ~2064x2208 per the skill's table, 11.11ms frame budget as stated, judder note), Interaction (grab for manipulation, point+click for UI/distant, physical toss, hand-tracking caveat about lower precision suiting casual audiences), Spatial Design (1 unit = 1 meter rule, within-arm's-reach layout, depth-cue priority stereo>parallax>shadows>occlusion), and the Anti-Patterns table rendered as a pass/fail checklist (player controls camera, maintain 90 FPS, large UI text, scale to reach). All numbers and techniques in the deliverable trace to the skill. No code execution, binary output, network or MCP/connector tools were needed or used.
